title: Moved to forge.fedoraproject.org
description:
It has been suggested by a Fedora community member that the Gitlab-hosted Fedora Legal repos be moved to Fedora Forge. 

I'm inclined to think this is a good idea conceptually because I don't like Gitlab for two reasons: (1) it's overengineered for our purposes and has what I think are various confusing or overly complex features or design choices and (2) it's open core.

What are the practical or other benefits of continuing to host this on Gitlab.com rather than Fedora Forge, other than inertia?

description:

```
 * In addition, as a special exception, Dom Lachowicz

 * non-LGPL Spelling Provider libraries (eg: a MSFT Office
 * spell checker backend) and distribute linked combinations including
 * the two.  You must obey the GNU Lesser General Public License in all

 * this file, you may extend this exception to your version of the
 * file, but you are not obligated to do so.  If you do not wish to
 * do so, delete this exception statement from your version.
```
https://github.com/rrthomas/enchant/blob/774ff6dc2e441ba2b9b786f8edbe00e014960408/lib/internal.vapi#L18

Scancode recognizes it as https://scancode-licensedb.aboutcode.org/spell-checker-exception-lgpl-2.1-plus
SPDX does not recognize it.

title: add man-pages-l10n as an exception to LicenseRef-MIT-CRL-Xim
description:
Opening an issue per https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/merge_requests/829#note_3123251283

The package `man-pages-l10n` contains localized man pages of various packages. The license of `man-pages-l10n` is constructed as concanation of the licenses of source packages. See https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/man-pages-l10n/blob/rawhide/f/man-pages-l10n.spec#_37

One of the package is `netpbm` that uses LicenseRef-MIT-CRL-Xim that is not-allowed, but the package got an exception in the past.
https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/blob/main/data/LicenseRef-MIT-CRL-Xim.toml?ref_type=heads#L39

I propose to grant man-pages-l10n the exception too.

title: Create XML or YAML files for LicenseRefs
description:
This issue is related to #225.

For better or worse, SPDX long ago settled on XML (and what I think is a poorly documented schema) for encoding its license data for identifiers and exceptions in the SPDX license list.

For typical LicenseRef identifiers in fedora-license-data, we have a single license text that is not in the SPDX license identifier list. We've been copying the license text into the TOML file for the LicenseRef. 

I've started working on some scanning tools. Because I've been writing some code that handles the canonical SPDX license-list-XML files, I realized that it would be helpful to have XML files for these LicenseRefs conforming to the SPDX schema (or a simple subset thereof) so that such tools (or tools written by others) could easily be used with such non-SPDX-license-list license data. So I think we should have a separate directory of XML files for these LicenseRefs. We would probably then not want to have the license text in the TOML file, so that normally no TOML file would have the `text` field populated.

Actually, given how annoying XML generally is and the SPDX use in particular, I am thinking we could have YAML files for this purpose that are equivalent to a subset of the SPDX XML.

```
The copyright in this software is being made available under the BSD License, 
included below. This software may be subject to other third party and 
contributor rights, including patent rights, and no such rights are granted 
under this license.
```

The TPM reference implementation is currently used upstream by the Coconut SVSM project (via the `tpm-20-ref @ bc29a21` git submodule link in https://github.com/coconut-svsm/svsm/tree/main/libtcgtpm/deps). This project is in the roadmap to be proposed for inclusion in Fedora as soon as the corresponding kernel code is merged.

Thus we need clarity on whether that TPM ref impl license can be considered a direct match for one of the existing SDPX BSD variants, or if the extra intro text effectively turns it into a new license (which may not be acceptable for Fedora)
